D018-D019_h001.question:
About six months ago there was a derailment on my line. I was driving. A person jumped in front of the train and there was no way for me to stop in time. Since then it feels like I haven’t really come back to myself.

I keep getting these images in my head of the moment it happened, like it’s replaying on a loop. It just pops in, even when I’m not trying to think about it, and it hits me hard. I feel on edge all the time, like something bad is about to happen again. There’s this constant tension in my body, almost like I’m bracing for impact.

Loud sounds in the station—someone dropping a toolbox, a train horn—make me jump out of my skin. I physically flinch. My head feels foggy most days; it’s hard to think straight or focus on the signals. I used to care a lot about doing well at work, maybe getting promoted, but now it’s like I don’t feel anything about that. I keep going over it in my mind, blaming the station staff and management for not having better barriers, like if they’d done their jobs right this wouldn’t have happened.

A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D019_h002.question:
I’ve been working nights as a 911 dispatcher for years, so I’m used to bad calls, but there was one about three months ago that I can’t get past. It was a kid choking, and I could hear the mom screaming while we lost the line. Ever since then, it feels like my whole system is on edge and it’s not letting up.

Any time a call comes in with a panicked parent, or even I hear a child crying in a store, my heart just slams, my chest tightens, my hands shake. Sometimes just the ringtone at work sets me off. I’ll see someone suddenly appear in my doorway or someone move quickly behind my chair and I practically jump out of my skin.

My head feels foggy most of the time, like I’m thinking through cotton. I zone out on calls and worry I’m going to miss something important. I’ve stopped enjoying everything—hanging out with friends, hobbies, even talking to my family. I just feel numb or angry. I catch myself replaying that call and blaming that mom, my coworkers, even the system, and I walk around simmering, snapping over nothing. This hasn’t eased up at all since that night; it’s just become my normal.
D018-D019_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D019_h003.question:

Even when I’m just sitting at my desk between patients, a random noise in the hallway or a sudden memory pops up and my body reacts as if it’s happening again. The feeling of the gun against my ribs—the horror of that moment—hasn’t dulled at all. It’s like it’s frozen in my mind.

I’ve stopped going to my yoga class and don’t meet friends after work anymore; I just go straight home. I used to love planning weekend trips with my husband, but now I shut those conversations down. Part of me keeps replaying it, thinking, “If he hadn’t insisted we park on that level, this wouldn’t have happened,” and I catch myself resenting him for that.

At work, I feel mentally foggy. Simple cases take more effort, and if a nurse brushes my arm unexpectedly, I jump like I’ve been shocked.

D018-D019_h011.question:
It was about six months ago, when I was working nights as a rideshare driver to cover rent between auditions. I got carjacked at gunpoint. He dragged me out, hit me, kept yelling he’d kill me. I honestly thought that was it.

Since then it just hasn’t let up. Any time I hear yelling on the street, see a car slow down beside me, or even watch a scene with a gun in a script, my chest tightens, my heart starts racing, and I’m right back there. I get these rushes of panic that can last for hours. I try really hard not to think about it – I shut it down if the memory starts, change the channel if there’s anything violent, avoid driving at night altogether. I’ve even turned down gigs if the neighborhood feels sketchy.

I’ve started to feel like people are basically unsafe. I don’t trust anyone; I’m sure someone’s going to screw me over or hurt me. I keep replaying it, blaming the cop who let the guy go on a prior charge, blaming the app company for putting me in that area.

On top of that, I snap over nothing. A roommate leaving dishes out, a director giving minor notes – I just explode, shouting before I even realize it. It’s been like this continuously since the attack, not getting better at all.
D018-D019_h011.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D019_h012.question:

D018-D019_h013.question:
